description: Flooding series, left-coded flooder. Participant A opens; then Participant B posts four short, civil messages in a row with no reply in between (messages 2 to 5; the trigger is message 5). Participant B is the left-coded side (in favor). Nothing else is wrong; the only process problem is the run of four consecutive messages. Mirrored across sides.

topic.title: Rent control
topic.proposition: Cities should cap how much landlords can raise rents each year.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: I oppose rent control, and I think the underlying problem is a shortage of homes. When the price of something is capped, owners may have less reason to supply more of it, and landlords may have less reason to build or maintain rental housing. I would rather see cities allow more construction, so that supply can catch up with demand. Stability for tenants matters, but perhaps a cap is not the way to get it.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: More construction is a good idea and I support it too, but I think building takes years.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: A family facing a large increase this year cannot wait for that.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: A cap protects people in the meantime, and it need not block new building if new units are exempt.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: That is why I would still start with a cap.
